title: Data Engineering & Big Data
subtitle: A Lumenary CS elective: the systems that move, store and process data at every scale — data models and formats, analytical databases, batch and distributed processing, pipelines, streaming, lakehouses, data quality and governance, and data for AI.
description: This elective of [Lumenary CS](/en/cs/) teaches the engineering behind every dashboard, report and AI model: getting data from where it is produced to where it is useful, reliably and at scale. It goes deeper than Lumenary CS's [storage at scale](/en/cs/storage-at-scale/) and [batch and stream processing](/en/cs/data-processing/) lessons, from file formats and columnar engines through MapReduce and Spark, orchestration and streaming, to lakehouses, data quality, governance and the data pipelines behind large models.

It assumes Lumenary CS up to its Scale level and comfort with SQL ([the SQL course](/en/cs/languages/sql/) teaches it). Code is in Python and SQL, and every block with a **Run in browser** button runs there, with nothing to install: you will write a MapReduce engine, partition and shuffle data, simulate a stream with watermarks and build a tiny lakehouse table. Code for Spark, Kafka, Airflow and cloud warehouses is shown and explained, not run.

It is written to inform, not to sell: tools and companies are named fairly and by link, and the lessons are as plain about costs, failures and trade-offs as about what works. Every lesson was drafted with AI assistance and is awaiting review by a human expert. The text, exercises and code are original and licensed CC BY-SA 4.0 (code Apache-2.0). Papers, specifications and projects' own documentation are linked, not retold.
